title: Who Is Allowed to Interpret a Dead Designer’s Codes?
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: No single record automatically grants the authority to interpret a dead designer’s codes: legal control, corporate office, curatorial custody, craft knowledge, family memory, community legitimacy, and audience recognition are different claims.
The dual designer attribution makes succession visible as an evidence question: house continuity does not erase uncertainty about individual authorship.

01 · CLAIM — What authority is being asserted?. Name the verb: preserve, exhibit, authenticate, reproduce, license, design, speak for, teach, sell, or change. Avoid the totalizing phrase “protect the legacy.”
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · RECORD — What supports that claim?. Attach corporate appointment, trademark record, license, will, probate order, copyright chain, collection agreement, employment record, oral history, craft evidence, or community protocol as appropriate.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · LIMIT — Where does the authority stop?. A museum accession does not appoint a house successor; inherited copyright does not confer craft mastery; corporate title does not erase community memory; cultural legitimacy does not itself transfer a registered asset.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · CONTEST — How can interpretation be challenged and revised?. Publish sources, acknowledge gaps, credit carriers, invite corrections, document dissent, and schedule periodic review rather than presenting succession as final truth.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 17 U.S.C. § 201 — Ownership of copyright is retained as evidence, education, reporting or rights context.
narrativeSequence.rights: Official statutory text; quote narrowly and link. Subsections (d) and (e) address transfer by law, will, or intestacy.

narrativeSequence.caption: Standard Application Help: Claimant — transfer by inheritance is retained as evidence, education, reporting or rights context.
narrativeSequence.rights: Official registration guidance; paraphrase and link. It does not resolve state probate or contract questions.

mapping.prompt: Choose one proposed act—exhibition, reissue, campaign, collection, authentication, or license.
List every legal, corporate, curatorial, craft, family, community, and audience authority affected.
Attach the record supporting each claim and write its boundary.
Create a dissent and correction protocol; send legal conclusions to counsel and cultural or conservation questions to the right specialists.
